records.summary: Instead of crafting everything alone, let players shape the world through their characters, actions, and backstories. ✔ Session Zero Worldbuilding: Work with players to establish key aspects of the world, such as factions, major conflicts, and historical events. ✔ Emergent Lore: Instead of pre-defining everything, allow lore to develop naturally through gameplay. ✔ Shared Narrative Authority: Rotate GM duties or give players storytelling tools to add world details (e.g., defining a townʼs history when arriving there). ✔ Player-Driven Factions: Let players create guilds, noble houses, or political movements that grow over time. 📌 Worldbuilding Tip: Give players a “Lore Token” they can spend to introduce a new fact about the world—this keeps collaboration structured yet spontaneous.

Not all settings need encyclopedias of lore. A minimalist approach focuses on core themes and player- driven discovery. ✔ Start with a Strong Premise:“A world where magic is slowly dying” or “A civilization built inside a massive creature.” ✔ Leave Gaps for Discovery: Donʼt define everything—allow room for interpretation and improvisation. ✔ Use Implied Lore: A single strange artifact, inscription, or NPC rumor can suggest a vast unseen history. ✔ Restrict Information: If the players only know what their characters know, mystery becomes a core part of the setting. 📌 Worldbuilding Tip: Challenge yourself to describe an entire setting in one paragraph—what are the most essential details?

When societies crumble, they leave behind remnants of the old world while forcing survivors to forge new ways of life. A well-designed post-apocalyptic setting blends realism with imaginative storytelling, creating a world where scarcity, survival, and adaptation define the experience. 🔻 What Happens When Societies Fall? Societal collapse doesnʼt happen overnight—itʼs a process influenced by political, economic, environmental, and technological factors. Understanding these dynamics helps create believable and immersive settings.

records.proposedName: Designing Post-Apocalyptic Worlds That Feel Plausible
records.summary: Every post-apocalyptic world has a reason for its ruin and distinct challenges for survival. To make your setting feel authentic, explore how remnants of the old world interact with new struggles.

✔ Warlord States – Ruled by the strongest, relying on conquest and extortion. ✔ Nomadic Tribes – Constantly moving, scavenging, and adapting to a hostile world. ✔ Religious Orders – Devoted to prophecy, old-world deities, or post-collapse cults. ✔ Tech Hoarders – Keepers of lost knowledge, maintaining ancient databases and machines. ✔ Eco-Communes – Focused on sustainability, rebuilding, and coexisting with nature. ✔ Underground Societies – Living in bunkers, tunnels, or vaults, isolated from surface dangers. 📌 Worldbuilding Tip:Avoid monocultures—not all survivors will react to collapse in the same way. Different regions should develop unique responses to hardship.

1.Dimensional Nodes: •Mechanics: Dimensional Nodes must be placed in stable zones within each reality. Nodes are physically anchored in each dimension and use a combination of energy signatures unique to each dimension.

◦ A Dimensional Node has a maximum reach of 2 dimensions in either direction from the anchor. For every additional dimension, the chance of instability increases by 15%. •Cost: Due to the immense energy demands, operating a node requires significant power— typically a power source equivalent to that found on capital ships. 2.Reality Beacons: •Mechanics: Reality Beacons are anchored in high-energy points within each dimension, typically needing matched resonant energy or unique technology keys to activate.

◦ Without stabilizers, each additional dimension adds a 25% distortion effect. Roll d100, and on a distortion result, the message becomes scrambled or garbled. ◦ With stabilizers, distortion drops to 5% per additional dimension. •Interference Risks: High-risk zones (chaos storms, reality anomalies) increase distortion by an additional 10% per layer.

records.proposedName: What It Means to Traverse the Multiverse
records.summary: Operating in the multiverse isnʼt just about hopping from world to world—itʼs about existing in an environment where possibility itself is tangible, layered, and ever-shifting. In Multiversal, adventurers are more than wanderers; they are quantum actors in an interconnected, fluid lattice of timelines, worlds, and branches. Every decision, every movement, and every interaction is potentially reflected in alternate forms across realities— sometimes subtly, sometimes catastrophically. Multiversal dynamics refer to the unique physics, metaphysics, and narrative implications of such a structure. They encompass: •Parallel realities and alternate timelines •Encountering or merging with versions of yourself •Navigating shifting fate currents •Traveling with others while desynced in reality •Moving between branches and resisting multiversal strain Unlike single-world campaigns, multiversal adventures demand a different kind of awareness. Every world has its own "rules," and some rules break when you're not from there. Syncing to a reality can grant power, while resisting its pull may protect your identity—or shred it.

•Membership grants access to advanced weapons, armor, vehicles, and information. •High-level characters may gain access to resources like mech usage or orbital support. So, you're ready to dive into the wild, wide world of portals, huh? You're in for a treat because this is where the real fun starts. Portals aren't just your average doorways; they're your ticket to the ultimate adventures that stretch beyond the imagination. Picture this: one minute you're chilling in a dragon's lair (you know, the usual), and the next, you're stepping through a swirling vortex into a realm where the sky rains cupcakes. Welcome to the section where we talk all things portals and pathways!

records.proposedName: Shadow Paths: Veiled Routes of Power and Peril
records.summary: Overview: Shadow Paths are elusive, intangible routes that exist in a state of semi-reality, accessible only under specific conditions or to those with the knowledge or power to unveil them. These paths may weave through the land of shadows, connect darkened doorways across vast distances, or overlay the mortal realm in such a way that travelers can move unseen and undetected by those not attuned to their presence. Discovery and Access: Uncovering a Shadow Path often requires ancient knowledge, a gift bestowed by shadowy entities, or a rare artifact that pierces the veil between light and darkness. Access might be granted only during certain lunar phases, in places where the barrier between worlds is thin, or through rituals that call upon the essence of shadows themselves. The entrance to a Shadow Path might manifest as a darkened alleyway that wasnʼt there before, a mirrorʼs reflection that reveals another world, or a forest shrouded in an unnatural mist. Traversal Experience: Traveling via a Shadow Path is a surreal and disorienting experience, where the familiar rules of time and space may not apply. The path might be shrouded in an impenetrable darkness, illuminated only by strange, phosphorescent flora or the eerie glow of spectral lights. Sounds might be muffled or distorted, and travelers may feel the unnerving sensation of being watched or followed. The journey requires not just physical movement but a mental and spiritual navigation through the darkness. Destinations and Encounters: The destinations reached through Shadow Paths can be as varied as the realms of night themselves, from hidden enclaves of shadow-walkers or secret chambers within ancient ruins, to eerie, parallel versions of the real world where the unseen forces of darkness hold sway. Encounters along these paths might include spirits lost in the shadows, creatures born of darkness, or other travelers who navigate the paths for their own inscrutable purposes.

records.proposedName: Goblin Holes: Pathways of Whispering Chaos
records.summary: Overview: Goblin Holes are a network of tunnels that stretch across the land, burrowing through dimensions and the fabric of reality where chaos has been magically stabilized by goblin sorcerers or engineers. These tunnels, seemingly mundane to the untrained eye, resonate with the latent power of chaos, making them unpredictable and dangerous to all but their goblin creators. The walls of these tunnels are alive with eerie sounds—whispers of the chaos that lies just beyond their bounds, murmuring secrets and temptations to those who dare to travel through them. Discovery and Access: Stumbling upon a Goblin Hole is often accidental, found in the depths of ancient forests, beneath decrepit ruins, or hidden within the dark corners of the world. Accessing these tunnels requires either the guidance of a goblin familiar with their secrets or the acquisition of a key or token, often a magical artifact imbued with the essence of chaos that goblins use to navigate and stabilize the tunnels for safe passage. Traversal Experience: Venturing into a Goblin Hole is not for the faint of heart. The air is thick with a sense of unease, and the walls seem to shift and murmur with voices that are not quite voices, speaking languages that sound almost comprehensible. The path is winding and disorienting, with the sensation that reality itself is thin here, and one wrong step could lead into the maw of chaos. Despite this, for those who know the way, travel through a Goblin Hole can significantly shorten journeys, popping out miles away or even in entirely different realms. Destinations and Consequences: The destinations reached through Goblin Holes can be as unpredictable as the tunnels themselves. While goblins use them to move swiftly between their hidden enclaves or to launch surprise raids, adventurers might find themselves emerging in unexpected locations, from the heart of goblin kingdoms to the edges of reality where the fabric of the world is frayed and strange wonders—or dangers—await.

“If ruin had a rhythm, Apogine would be its echo. If silence had a shape, it would be built from the bones of this world.” Apogine is not just a planet—it is the final breath of a reality that refused to die. Suspended in the branch of Silentium, Apogine orbits a solitary star beneath a sky devoid of galaxies, moons, or constellations. Its lonely sun gives off a dull and dying light, and the one pale moon that drifts above offers no guidance. It is the last remnant of a universe where everything else has already faded. What defines Apogine is not war, nor magic, nor monsters—but inevitability. Civilizations rise not to flourish, but to collapse with grandeur. Cities are built from the bones of cities built from the bones of cities. Each structure, belief, or power that takes root here is doomed to end, and the residents know this. Whatʼs remarkable is not that things fall apart—but that something always rises again from the rubble, clinging to meaning in the face of total erasure. Apogine is the polar node of the Silentium branch, embodying the full weight of entropy, psychological erosion, and environmental decline. It is one of the most isolated points in the entire multiverse. There are no portals in or out. Even Translimina, the chaotic layer between realities, is shattered and silent beneath its crust. The only known path leads through Garrockʼs Tunnel, a staggering journey of years through the Chaos & Foam. Despite its fatalistic pull, Apogine is not lifeless. Two species dominate its ruins: the Rog, decadent pigfolk clinging to the illusion of empire and opulence; and the Furashin, rodent-like survivors who adapt to every apocalyptic cycle with agility and cunning. Around them swirl echoes of extinct empires, collapsed philosophies, and haunting remnants of technologies that once tried to resist decay.

records.proposedName: The Godmetal Vein That Birthed an Empire
records.summary: “He was a miner. A broken goblin with calloused hands and a voice no one followed. Then the world split open, and every goblin alive heard him scream.” There are no natural portals on Apogine. No gate spells. No stable Translimina veins. The world is sealed—until, one day, it wasnʼt. That breach was not a miracle, but a byproduct of ancient divinity buried in planetary flesh. That breach is known as Garrockʼs Tunnel.

records.proposedName: High Skyseer Luraen, Chronicles of the Fractured Sky
records.summary: Dionasia is a shattered world suspended in a delicate balance of awe and ruin. Once a thriving planet of advanced civilizations and technomantic marvels, it was broken by its own ambition in an event now known as The Great Fracturing. In the aftermath, gravity inverted, cities collapsed, and the laws of nature twisted around divine intervention. What remained became an impossible landscape of floating cliffs, inverted waterfalls, and skyward abysses. Now, life clings to the edges—literally. Civilization persists in the form of hanging cities, suspended from craggy cliffs and overhanging mountainsides, held together not by tectonics but by immense floating anchors known as Gravity Wells. These Wells are not only physical stabilizers but spiritual symbols— remnants of the god Aserʼs mercy, who prevented the complete dissolution of the world. Dionasiaʼs skies are not the heavens above, but the void below. Falling is not a fall to earth, but an ascension into endless blue. Travel is a careful dance across pulleys, cables, domesticated flying beasts, and precarious bridges. Up is down, down is death—and gravity is never constant. The people of Dionasia—be they city-dwellers, nomads of the skies, forest mystics, or ravine scavengers —live with a cultural memory steeped in humility and caution. Ancient ruins of the technomage age still hang above the abyss, offering lost knowledge and buried danger. The Faith of the Fractured Sky shapes daily life with rituals of penance, awe, and devotion to the twin deities Diona and Aser. Prophets known as Mystic Skywalkers meditate on cliff edges to receive divine visions from the Wells. Dionasia is a setting of inverted physics, reverent wonder, and dangerous beauty. Ideal for campaigns centered on exploration, spirituality, technological rediscovery, or survival in treacherous environments, it challenges players to rethink orientation, risk, and reverence.

•Anchor Emergency: A cityʼs anchor is failing—players must repair it before the entire lower tier is lost. •Rite of the Lanterns: A festival interrupted by a skybeast attack or divine vision. •City on the Move: A sky-faring nomadic settlement approaches, threatening trade routes or offering vital aid. •Class Revolt: A faction from the lower tiers rises up, seeking equality or revenge. •Echo Catacombs: Exploration of old technomage tunnels reveals ancient secrets and dangerous constructs. Dionasiaʼs cities are more than settlements—they are philosophies built into stone and sky. Each Hanging City is a monument to survival, belief, and defiance in a world that fell upward.

records.proposedName: The Faith of the Fractured Sky
records.summary: After the world shattered, faith became both an anchor and a map. Dionasiaʼs fractured heavens and inverted laws gave rise to deeply spiritual traditions rooted in awe, fear, and cosmic reconciliation. Most Dionasians follow some interpretation of the dominant religion known as The Faith of the Fractured Sky, though localized beliefs, mystic orders, and divergent sects thrive in parallel.

The Faith of the Fractured Sky tells the story of a once-whole world and the gods who watched over it— Diona, the Divine Architect of Order, and Aser, the Guardian of Mercy and Change. Skybeast Attacks Predatory raids from the abyss or high- altitude nests
